project_type: Node.js ESM monorepo — Dema: a deterministic constitutional execution engine with replayable receipts. Zero runtime dependencies, consent-bound, receipt-backed. 25 workspace packages under packages/.
language: JavaScript (ESM, type:module), Node >= 20. A governed Rust runtime is referenced as the production executor (JS gateway retired by design).
build_system: npm workspaces. No node_modules present at session start and none required to run tests (zero runtime deps). bin/dema is the CLI entrypoint.
test_framework: node --test with TAP reporter, wrapped by scripts/ci/run-with-classifier.mjs which captures the true child exit and runs scripts/ci/classify-known-harness-failures.mjs (the G8 gate). The G8 gate fails CLOSED on any 'not ok' line whose test NAME is not on the KNOWN_MASKABLE allowlist AND whose diagnostic block does not carry an environmental CAUSE signature (EROFS/EPERM/ENOENT). Masking by name alone is explicitly forbidden by the hardening.
build_command: No separate build for the JS test path. (DEMA production UI build and the governed Rust runtime are out of scope for this slice.)
test_command: npm test  (runs node --test --test-reporter=tap tests/*.test.js through the G8 classifier). Per-file: node --test tests/<file>.test.js
verification_instructions: 1) Run the three affected files in isolation and confirm 0 failures (permission-dependent assertions become skips with an honest reason, not passes). 2) Run full `npm test` and confirm the G8 classifier reports a clean/allowlisted run (exit 0) with 0 UNRECOGNIZED failures. 3) Confirm the skip reason strings are honest and that the assertions still run (and still pass) on a mode-enforcing (non-root) environment such as CI ubuntu-latest.
snapshot_or_generated_files: docs/claims/PUBLIC_CLAIMS.generated.md is generated via `npm run claims:generate`. AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md are generated projections (DO NOT EDIT). None of these are produced by this slice.
setup_instructions: No install needed to run the JS tests. Node 22.23.3, npm 11.4.2, cargo 1.92 are present. The suite runs as root (uid=0) in this sandbox.
environment_constraints: VERIFIED CRITICAL CONSTRAINT: the sandbox runs the test suite as root (uid=0). Root bypasses DAC permission bits, so chmod-based fault injection is a NO-OP: `cat` of a 0o000 file succeeds and writing into a 0o500 dir succeeds (both demonstrated empirically). This defeats the permission-based fault-injection seams in exactly three test files and produces 25 'failures' that are environmental, NOT code defects. CI runs on GitHub ubuntu-latest (non-root 'runner' user) where these same tests PASS. No non-root user with uid>=1000 exists in the sandbox; node lives under /root/.nvm so it cannot be exec'd as 'nobody'. Network: assume restricted; not needed for this slice.
contribution_requirements: BIZRA law (CONTRIBUTING.md): No claim without proof; No action without consent; No memory without boundary; No monetization without verified benefit. PR checklist: tests included, no hidden background process, consent boundary explicit, no token/economic claims. No-false-GREEN discipline is enforced mechanically by the G8 classifier — a skip is honest; masking a real-looking assertion failure by name alone is forbidden.
key_patterns: CANONICAL IN-REPO PRECEDENT for this exact situation: tests/first-encounter-admission.test.js defines `const canEnforceModes = async (fsp, dir, path) => { await fsp.chmod(path, 0o000); try { await fsp.readdir(path); return false; } catch { return true; } finally { await fsp.chmod(path, 0o755); } }` and, when modes are not enforced, calls `t.skip("filesystem does not enforce modes for this process"); return;`. The fix MUST mirror this pattern: probe whether the running identity/filesystem actually enforces the specific permission the test relies on, and if not, skip that assertion with an honest reason — never fake a pass and never weaken the classifier.
